description: One-octave keyboard controller with pitch, gate and velocity outputs, which can be chained left to right to make a longer keyboard

params.text: Raises the base octave of the keyboard; it has no effect while a cable is patched to the OCT input
Lowers the base octave of the keyboard; it has no effect while a cable is patched to the OCT input
Steps the full-scale velocity voltage through 10V, 5V, 1V, two semitones and one semitone
Unipolar in the bottom position runs the velocity from 0V to the maximum; bipolar in the top position runs it from minus the maximum to plus the maximum

inputs.text: Gate from a keyboard up the chain, passed to the GATE output when the last key pressed was on that module
Pitch from a keyboard up the chain, passed to the CV output when the last key pressed was on that module
Sets the base octave from a voltage, 0V for octave 0 up to 9V for octave 9; voltages in between are floored and voltages outside the range are clamped
Velocity from a keyboard up the chain, passed to the VEL output when the last key pressed was on that module

outputs.text: Gate of the key being held, on this keyboard or one up the chain
Pitch of the last key pressed, on this keyboard or one up the chain
The base octave of this keyboard plus one volt, for the OCT input of the next keyboard in the chain
Velocity of the last key pressed, set by how far down the key it was clicked and scaled by the MAX VEL and BIPOL settings

notes: keyboards are chained with cables: patch the CV, GATE and VEL outputs of the keyboard on the left into the matching inputs here, and its OCT output into this module's OCT input
menu: Inverted velocity range — puts maximum velocity at the top of the keys instead of the bottom
Link velocity settings from left — copies the maximum velocity, the polarity and the inversion from the keyboard to the left; the panels must touch, with no gap between them
Tracer — keeps the last key pressed faintly lit
CV input viewer — stops the module responding to key presses and instead lights the key matching the CV input, turning a chain of keyboards into a note display

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
